english.title: Sponsor fail give written notice of urgent safety measures

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Medicines for Human Use Clinical Trials Regulations 2004

english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being the sponsor of a clinical trial for which urgent safety measures were taken in order to protect the subjects of the trial against an immediate hazard to their health or safety, failed to give written notice to the licensing authority, namely **(..SPECIFY THE LICENSING AUTHORITY..), and the relevant ethics committee, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ETHICS COMMITTEE..), of the measures taken and the circumstances giving rise to those measures immediately and in any event no later than 3 days from the date the measures were taken
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 30(2)(b), 49(1)(f) and 52 of the Medicines for Human Use (ClinicalTrials) Regulations 2004.

english.notes:
(i) Regulation 51 of the of the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004 provides a defence of due diligence.
(ii) This offence no longer applies from the 27th April 2026 due to changes made by the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) (Amendment) Regulations 2025. For the offence applicable after this date, see H102700.
